items.title: PALMER OR ROGERS?! 🔵 | Sam's GW4 Transfer Round-Up
items.headline: Morgan Rogers edges Cole Palmer as Chelsea’s value buy despite cup impact
items.summary:
Liverpool and Chelsea dominate the transfer market this week, but the biggest buying trends carry different levels of risk. Cody Gakpo leads all arrivals with more than 590,000 transfers in, ahead of Alexander Isak on 434,000, yet Gakpo is flagged after missing Liverpool’s Champions League match. That absence makes his huge ownership rush a potential concern until there is clearer fitness news.

Morgan Rogers is the second most-bought player, attracting more than 528,000 transfers, while Cole Palmer is fourth on over 422,000. Both are heavily backed after their League Cup involvement: although rested from the start, they change the match after coming on at half-time. Rogers produces a hat-trick of assists and is considered unlucky not to receive another Fantasy assist, while Palmer scores twice.

The strong returns make the choice between the two Chelsea options difficult, but Rogers is the preferred transfer this week. Palmer offers the greater premium upside after his two goals, but the £2.0m saving on Rogers is judged more valuable for squad structure. Managers buying into Chelsea’s attack are therefore advised to take Rogers as the efficient route, while monitoring Gakpo’s flag before joining the Liverpool transfer rush.
key_points: Cody Gakpo is the most transferred-in player this week with more than 590,000 arrivals, but his flag after missing the Champions League match adds fitness risk.
Alexander Isak is the third most-bought player, with more than 434,000 managers bringing him in.
Morgan Rogers is the second most transferred-in player on over 528,000 purchases.
Rogers comes off the bench at half-time in the League Cup and registers three assists, with a possible fourth Fantasy assist also noted.
Cole Palmer also enters at half-time and scores twice, reinforcing his premium appeal.
Rogers is the recommended Chelsea buy over Palmer because he costs £2.0m less while still showing major attacking involvement.

items.title: FPL GW4 COMPLETE GUIDE ⁉️ FINAL THOUGHTS ON CHELSEA & ARSENAL! 🤔 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Cole Palmer leads Gameweek 4 captaincy as Chelsea target Hull at Stamford Bridge
items.summary:
Chelsea’s home meeting with Hull dominates Gameweek 4. Hull remain unbeaten defensively and rank well for big chances conceded, but their expected-goals-conceded data is less convincing and Chelsea’s six-goal cup display strengthens the case for a home breakthrough. Chelsea are expected to score two or three, although there is a meaningful risk that Hull keep the game tight and limit the upside. Cole Palmer is the preferred one-week attacking buy and captain because of his haul potential, penalty involvement and the fixture; João Pedro is the best long-term Chelsea asset thanks to his lower price, forward classification and strong all-season appeal. Morgan Rogers is a viable cheaper alternative, but Palmer is favoured for the immediate ceiling.

A Chelsea attacking triple-up of Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers is defensible, particularly for a Free Hit, but is not essential beyond Gameweek 4. Brentford away follows before Bournemouth and Everton, so two Chelsea attackers is the more balanced long-term approach. Bruno Fernandes to Palmer and Bryan Mbeumo to Rogers are recommended free transfers, but not moves worth taking a minus-four for. Managers needing hits to reshape their squad should instead consider a Wildcard, especially as selling Bruno frees substantial funds to improve multiple positions. Bruno is expected to be fit despite being seen with the Manchester United physio after midweek European action.

Arsenal’s defensive strength remains a major theme after their 1-0 Champions League win over Napoli. Riccardo Calafiori is the leading Arsenal pick: he is rested in midweek, likely to start, offers clean-sheet potential and ranks highly for Arsenal expected goal involvement. A defensive double-up is attractive, with Gabriel the superior points pick over Ezri Konsa but Konsa’s £4.4m price making him exceptional value while Timber and Mosquera remain unavailable or not ready to start. Bukayo Saka and Gabriel offer maximum individual upside, while Martin Ødegaard and Konsa create a cheaper structure that can fund upgrades such as Yoane Wissa to Alexander Isak.

Palmer is the top captain, ahead of João Pedro, Isak, Erling Haaland and Rogers. Chelsea have the highest projected goal total of the week, while Palmer is projected as the highest-scoring individual; João Pedro has the strongest goal-or-assist probability. Isak against Fulham and Haaland away to Manchester United are strong alternatives, with the derby expected to be open and high scoring. A Palmer Triple Captain is viable but not preferred unless managers are fully committed: Hull’s defensive resilience creates downside, and future premium opportunities include favourable home fixtures for Haaland and later fixtures for Palmer. Liverpool assets are less appealing amid doubts over Cody Gakpo and fitness management for Barcola, while Dominik Szoboszlai is the safest midfield route if investing in Liverpool.

For Wildcards, the preferred core includes David Raya, Calafiori, Konsa, Kaoru Mitoma’s replacement option Diego Gómez/Kadioglu-type budget defenders as applicable, Palmer, Rogers, Pascal Groß, Mbeumo, Wissa, João Pedro and Haaland. Raya is the top goalkeeper option, though a £4.5m keeper such as Kinsky or Verbruggen can release funds for Saka. In the immediate XI, start attacking players such as Groß, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Mbeumo and Calafiori over lower-upside defenders; Calvert-Lewin’s 90-minute security and penalties make him a clear start against Newcastle. Newcastle defenders are less appealing away to Leeds, while Brighton and Leeds defenders rotate well with Newcastle for future fixture coverage.
key_points: Captain Cole Palmer against Hull, with João Pedro as vice-captain; Isak and Haaland are the leading non-Chelsea alternatives.
Buy Palmer for Bruno Fernandes and Rogers for Bryan Mbeumo only with free transfers; avoid a minus-four and consider a Wildcard if several changes are needed.
João Pedro is the best long-term Chelsea asset, while Palmer is the preferred short-term fixture target and highest-upside captain.
Limit Chelsea to two attackers for most squads, as Hull can frustrate them and Chelsea’s following fixtures are not strong enough to demand a long-term attacking triple-up.
Riccardo Calafiori is the standout Arsenal asset after his midweek rest, with Gabriel the premium defensive partner and £4.4m Ezri Konsa the value alternative.
Saka and Gabriel maximise Arsenal points potential, but Ødegaard and Konsa offer a cheaper structure that helps fund premium forwards such as Isak.
Avoid buying Cody Gakpo while he is a fitness doubt; Szoboszlai is the safer Liverpool midfield selection for Fulham at home.
Save the Triple Captain unless fully convinced by Palmer, as Hull’s defence adds risk and better Haaland or Palmer fixtures remain later in the season.

items.title: LATEST INJURY + TEAM NEWS 🚨 | FPL GW4 |  FPL Tips 2026/27
items.headline: Start De Cuyper as Gakpo faces a major Gameweek 4 fitness doubt
items.summary:
Cody Gakpo is the standout selection concern ahead of Gameweek 4. The Liverpool forward misses the midweek match against Atletico Madrid, does not train on Thursday and needs a successful final session to make the squad for Fulham. With such a short turnaround and no training during the week, he is considered unlikely to start; managers with a playable replacement are advised to bench him rather than risk a one-point substitute appearance. Brighton's De Cuyper is specifically backed as a strong replacement this week, even if his longer-term security becomes less convincing when Pervis Estupinan, Kaoru Mitoma and other Brighton options return.

Chelsea attackers remain attractive for Hull at home, but Moises Caicedo is still unavailable, while Pstra, Omega and Henderson also remain out. Romeo Lavia is fit after being rested in midweek. Elsewhere, Nathan Collins misses Brentford's trip to Bournemouth with a calf injury and is not expected back until after the international break. Everton midfielder Christian Norgaard is also out beyond the break, while Tottenham's new signing Mudryk has an ankle injury that is expected to rule him out for six to eight weeks. James Maddison is back in Spurs training and could return against Everton, whereas Dejan Kulusevski is still being managed and is unlikely to feature.

Arsenal assets receive encouraging news before Sunderland away: Ben White is fit despite appearing to limp off against Napoli, and Mikel Arteta reports no fresh injuries from that match. Jurrien Timber is nearing a matchday return, potentially in the cup before the international break, while Mosquera may also return soon; that raises future rotation risk for White and fellow defenders, particularly around Gameweek 6 wildcard plans. Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri is available again after a back issue, but managers should separate fitness from starting security for the Manchester derby. City may use a more conservative midfield or attack at Old Trafford, leaving Turkey's place uncertain, although he remains worth holding because even reduced minutes could bring returns against a vulnerable United defence.

The broader transfer approach is to avoid unnecessary short-term moves before the international break unless an injured player leaves no viable bench cover. De Cuyper and White are useful immediate starters but are viewed as potential Gameweek 6 wildcard sales because of returning competition. Liverpool's Gakpo is the more urgent call: start a reliable alternative if possible. Newcastle's Ded is another late fitness watch after coming off with hamstring discomfort against Millwall, although the club suggests the issue is not serious and offers little detailed injury information.
key_points: Bench Cody Gakpo for a reliable substitute if possible, as he has not trained ahead of Liverpool's Gameweek 4 match with Fulham and is unlikely to start.
Start Brighton's De Cuyper if Gakpo is absent; he is a strong short-term option but faces longer-term competition when Brighton's injured players return.
Ben White is fit for Arsenal's trip to Sunderland, though Timber and Mosquera nearing returns increase Arsenal defensive rotation risk after the break.
Hold Turkey for Manchester City at Manchester United if he is otherwise a starter in your squad, despite uncertainty over whether he starts the derby.
Nathan Collins is out for Brentford until after the international break with a calf injury, while Christian Norgaard remains absent for Everton.
Tottenham's Mudryk is ruled out for around six to eight weeks, but James Maddison returns to training and may feature against Everton.
Avoid forcing transfers before the international break when you have playable cover; Gameweek 6 is highlighted as a natural wildcard point for owners of De Cuyper and White.
Monitor Newcastle's Ded late: his hamstring discomfort is described as precautionary, but the club is unlikely to provide detailed updates.

items.title: FPL GW4 Final Thoughts 🔥 Team News 🚨 Triple Captain Palmer 🤔
items.headline: Cole Palmer edges João Pedro for Gameweek 4 captaincy as triple-captain call looms
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the preferred Gameweek 4 captain for Chelsea’s home match against Hull, narrowly ahead of João Pedro. Palmer is expected to start after playing only 45 minutes in midweek, takes penalties and offers the extra midfielder scoring point, while his lower ownership makes him a more valuable differential. The Triple Captain chip is under serious consideration: Hull is a favourable fixture and Palmer should receive 80-plus minutes, although saving the chip for Erling Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7 or Hull in Gameweek 16 remains viable. Haaland’s schedule is busy, but he is still expected to start against Ipswich rather than be rested for it.

The planned squad move is Cherki to Morgan Rogers, with the remaining free transfer rolled. The starting XI features Raya, Calafiori, Kiwior and Kaoru Mitoma’s temporary replacement Kaiper in defence; Palmer, Rogers, Szoboszlai and Groß in midfield; and João Pedro, Haaland and Wissa up front. Triple Arsenal defence is considered playable away to Sunderland, while Kaiper is worth starting against Coventry with Mitoma still unavailable until after the international break. The only bench-order uncertainty is between Lewis Hall and Sangaré, with Hall safer for minutes but Sangaré carrying a potentially better attacking upside.

Arsenal’s Ben White is fit for Gameweek 4 and should be started, but his longer-term security may become less comfortable if Jurrien Timber returns after the international break. Kiwior is still expected to remain ahead of Mosquera at centre-back. At Liverpool, Gakpo is a Gameweek 4 doubt and should not be bought, wildcarded in or used on a Free Hit; current owners can start him only if their bench is weak, as a late substitute appearance is possible. Liverpool’s fixtures after Fulham are merely acceptable, so selling Gakpo for Morgan Rogers or Morgan Gibbs-White is reasonable rather than urgent.

The advice is to avoid chasing uncertain minutes. Nico O’Reilly and Josko Gvardiol are bench-and-reassess options as Manchester City’s selection at left-back becomes harder to predict, while Newcastle’s Dan Burn is a risk after a hamstring issue and Lewis Hall is the preferred Newcastle defensive buy. Brighton’s Kaiper is a good short-term hold but not an ideal new wildcard selection because Arsenal follow Coventry; Vuskovic is viewed as the safer longer-term Brighton defender. Jack Grealish may be ready to start for Everton, but it is better to wait for confirmation, with Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall the safer similarly priced option.

An early Gameweek 4 wildcard is favoured over waiting until Gameweek 6 if the squad already needs repair. The key targets—Haaland, Chelsea attackers and Arsenal assets—remain broadly the same, and several attractive fixtures arrive before Gameweek 6. Martin Ødegaard is backed at £6.7m despite unsustainably strong early output and some rotation risk, while Szoboszlai is preferred long term to Gibbs-White because the £0.9m saving is useful and Szoboszlai has set pieces and likely penalties. If choosing between Isak plus Ødegaard or Bukayo Saka plus Barry, Isak and Ødegaard are preferred as a pair, though Saka is still rated above Isak in isolation.
key_points: Captain Cole Palmer against Hull in Gameweek 4, with João Pedro the closest alternative; Palmer’s penalties, midfield scoring and lower ownership give him the edge.
Triple Captain Palmer is a credible differential play, but Haaland at home to Ipswich in Gameweek 7 remains the more obvious future alternative.
Roll a transfer after moving Cherki to Morgan Rogers, unless late team news creates a new problem.
Start Ben White in Gameweek 4, but monitor Timber’s return as White may become a sell consideration after the international break.
Do not buy Gakpo while he is an injury doubt; owners can bench him if they have cover or sell to Rogers or Gibbs-White without major regret.
Bench Nico O’Reilly and reassess in Gameweek 5 rather than buying him, as competition with Gvardiol and City’s midfield options clouds his minutes.
Prefer Lewis Hall over Dan Burn among Newcastle defenders, with Burn carrying a hamstring concern and Livramento a future minutes threat.
Wildcard in Gameweek 4 rather than waiting for Gameweek 6 if needed, as Chelsea, Arsenal and Haaland are desirable targets now rather than after the break.

items.title: FPL GW4 Best Wildcard Team (According to FPL Experts) #fpl
items.headline: Calafiori and Cancelo dominate expert Gameweek 4 Wildcard drafts
items.summary:
A composite of 35 expert Gameweek 4 Wildcard squads points to Kinski as the leading goalkeeper choice, appearing in 37% of drafts. Raya and Verbruggen are the main alternatives, but Kinski narrowly wins the consensus vote, suggesting experts are prioritising his value and immediate appeal over the more established premium options.

Defence is built around Calafiori and Cancelo, who each feature in 97% of the expert Wildcard teams and are the clearest near-unanimous picks. Egan is also heavily backed at 71%. The remaining squad slots include Mitrovic and Haaland, underlining Haaland's continuing status as a foundational FPL asset even when managers use a Wildcard to reshape their teams.

In midfield, Palmer and Rodgers are the most popular Chelsea selections, while Pascal Groß appears in 66% of squads. Szoboszlai and Saka fall below the 50% mark but remain prominent options, offering routes into Liverpool and Arsenal attacks for managers prepared to spend more or target higher-upside midfield spots. The forward line is led by João Pedro and Haaland, with Wissa most commonly used as the bench forward; Barry and Gonçalo are alternative budget-striker considerations.

The overall Wildcard template favours high-consensus defensive picks, Chelsea midfield exposure and a Haaland-led attack, while leaving flexibility around goalkeeper, the final midfield place and the cheaper forward slot. Wissa is the least popular of the main three forwards, making him the most obvious place to deviate from the combined expert squad.
key_points: Kinski is the most selected Gameweek 4 Wildcard goalkeeper at 37%, ahead of Raya and Verbruggen.
Calafiori and Cancelo appear in 97% of the expert Wildcard teams, making them the standout defensive template picks.
Egan is selected by 71% of experts and is the next most widely backed defensive option.
Palmer and Rodgers are the leading Chelsea midfield picks, while Pascal Groß features in 66% of squads.
Szoboszlai and Saka are still popular midfield options despite appearing in fewer than half of the Wildcard drafts.
Haaland and João Pedro lead the preferred forward line, with Wissa usually occupying the bench role.
Barry and Gonçalo offer alternatives to Wissa for managers seeking a different cheap-forward combination.

items.headline: Cole Palmer gets the armband after Bruno Fernandes downgrade ahead of Hull at home
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the focal point for Gameweek 4 after arriving in place of Bruno Fernandes, with the new signing immediately handed captaincy for Hull at home. João Pedro and Erling Haaland are the main alternatives, but Palmer's home fixture currently gives him the edge despite the obvious upside of Haaland.

Three transfers are already locked in. Fernandes becomes Palmer, while Solly March is upgraded to Morgan Gibbs-White rather than Morgan Rogers. Gibbs-White is selected partly with Nottingham Forest's Gameweek 5 home match against Coventry in mind, giving the squad a short-term fixture target before a likely Wildcard in Gameweek 6. The third move replaces the injured Joe Rodon, who is expected to be out for a couple of months, with defensive cover in the Mepham/Ben Mee mould.

Bart Verbruggen starts over Caoimhín Kelleher in goal, based on the view that Coventry are a weaker opponent than Everton, although there is little confidence in the call after previous goalkeeper decisions have gone badly. The defence features Arsenal's Gabriel, Brentford's Kristoffer Ajer away to Bournemouth, and the new replacement defender. Ben Mee is particularly attractive as a short-term option because of home matches against Newcastle and Crystal Palace before Gameweek 6, combining squad depth, possible clean sheets and some set-piece threat.

Bryan Mbeumo is retained despite facing Manchester City, beating Pascal Groß for the final midfield spot even though Groß has Coventry away. Mbeumo's strong start to the season outweighs the difficult fixture. The forward line is João Pedro, Carlton Morris and Haaland, while the team is built to hold together for two more rounds before using the Wildcard during the long international break ahead of Gameweek 6. A Wildcard this week is considered as a way to reverse transfers and build team value, but saving it offers greater scope to reshape the squad later.
key_points: Cole Palmer replaces Bruno Fernandes and is captained for Hull at home in Gameweek 4.
Morgan Gibbs-White arrives for Solly March, with Coventry at home in Gameweek 5 a key reason for choosing him over Morgan Rogers.
Joe Rodon's long-term injury forces a defensive transfer, with Mepham/Ben Mee providing depth ahead of Gameweek 6.
Bart Verbruggen starts over Caoimhín Kelleher in goal despite uncertainty over the goalkeeper call.
Bryan Mbeumo keeps his place against Manchester City ahead of Pascal Groß, whose fixture is Coventry away.
Erling Haaland and João Pedro remain captaincy alternatives to Palmer.
The Wildcard is likely saved for Gameweek 6, after the international break, rather than used to undo the confirmed transfers now.

items.title: FPL GW4 FINAL WILDCARD | 30k Rank Team Selection 🔥 My Squad & Captain
items.headline: Haaland, Palmer and Saka anchor a Gameweek 4 Wildcard built for flexibility
items.summary:
A Gameweek 4 Wildcard resets a side that scored 49 points in Gameweek 3, with Erling Haaland’s Triple Captain producing only nine points despite more than 1.0 xG and 1.41 expected goals on target against Coventry. The underlying numbers still support Haaland, while near-misses for Riccardo Calafiori, Dominik Szoboszlai and Pascal Groß reinforce the view that the poor week is largely variance rather than a reason to abandon the core picks. Haaland remains the premium forward around whom the new squad is built, with João Pedro joining him up front as an exceptional value pick who is considered close to premium quality regardless of price.

The preferred goalkeeper is Tottenham’s 4.5m Kinsky rather than David Raya, freeing Arsenal slots and money for outfield players. The case rests on Spurs’ defensive improvement: excluding the Brentford defeat, they have conceded low expected-goals totals against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest, while their late-season record under De Zerbi is cited as the league’s best for non-penalty xG conceded. The defence is led by attacking Arsenal asset Calafiori and a 4.4m Arsenal centre-back expected to retain his place while William Saliba is absent, with budget defenders selected for defensive-contribution points and playable rotation fixtures. Newcastle’s Hall and Coventry’s Thomas are attractive bench options, while Thomas offers set-piece threat as well as clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles.

The five-man midfield is Cole Palmer, Bukayo Saka, Morgan Rogers, Szoboszlai and Groß. Chelsea’s attacking form drives the Palmer-Rogers double-up, particularly ahead of Hull, and Rogers’ three assists in the League Cup strengthen confidence in his role. Saka is preferred over Martin Ødegaard because his higher price gives easier routes to Bruno Fernandes, Phil Foden, Mbeumo and other emerging midfield options; he also retains penalty and set-piece appeal. Szoboszlai is the sole Liverpool pick despite Fulham at home being appealing, as the following fixtures are less convincing and his set pieces, defensive contributions and long-term minutes make him more fixture-proof than Liverpool’s pricier attackers. Groß is the reliable 5.5m enabler, with corners, penalties, box arrivals and secure 90-minute starts outweighing concerns about his age.

Everton striker Barry is the key rotating bench forward, with Ipswich and Hull in Gameweeks 5 and 6 standing out. He ranks just behind Haaland for xG so far, is now expected to have secure minutes as Everton’s only recognised striker, and may inherit penalties following Idrissa Gueye’s departure. Barry rotates with Groß and the defenders through difficult fixtures, while Gonzalo is a possible later upgrade from Gameweek 6. The overall Wildcard avoids excessive bench spending but aims to provide a dependable first substitute every week, allowing transfers to be saved for fixture swings, injuries or moves into midfielders such as Fernandes and Foden.
key_points: Wildcard in Gameweek 4 is built around Haaland and João Pedro up front, with Haaland the standout premium captaincy option despite his Gameweek 3 blank.
Kinsky is preferred as a 4.5m goalkeeper over Raya because Spurs’ recent defensive data is strong and the saving preserves Arsenal outfield slots.
Calafiori remains a priority Arsenal defender because of his advanced role, two early assists and a disallowed Gameweek 3 goal.
Palmer and Rogers form a Chelsea attacking double-up ahead of Hull, with Chelsea’s spread of goals and Rogers’ League Cup creativity supporting the move.
Saka is selected over Ødegaard for penalties, set pieces and price flexibility to switch into Fernandes, Foden, Mbeumo or other midfield options.
Szoboszlai is the only Liverpool asset, valued for set pieces, defensive contributions and fixture-proof routes to points while Liverpool’s run after Fulham is less appealing.
Groß is a long-term 5.5m hold due to penalties, corners, open-play involvement and reliable 90-minute starts, but rotates out for Barry in harder fixtures.
Barry is a budget Everton forward to target against Ipswich and Hull in Gameweeks 5-6, with strong xG, secure minutes and possible penalty duties.

items.title: My Team Selection for Gameweek 4 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Cole Palmer keeps captaincy as Arsenal defensive triple targets Sunderland clean sheet
items.summary:
Cole Palmer remains captain for Gameweek 4, with his differential appeal over João Pedro strengthening the case despite Pedro's strong form. Erling Haaland is untouchable in the forward line and is already earmarked for the armband in Gameweek 5, when Manchester City host Sunderland.

The defence is heavily committed to Arsenal, with David Raya, Calafiori and Conso forming a triple-up aimed at Sunderland's visit. De Cuyper completes the back line and retains appeal because he is still operating at left wing, a role expected to continue until Kaoru Mitoma returns.

The early transfer is Rayan Cherki to Morgan Rogers, completed before Rogers rises to £7.6m. Cherki is not viewed as a poor asset, but concerns over his minutes make Rogers the more secure and attractive option both for this week and longer term. Dominik Szoboszlai is kept for Fulham's weak defence, while Gross also has a favourable Coventry fixture.

João Pedro is backed for Hull at home and beyond, while Yoane Wissa survives despite disappointing in Gameweek 3. Wissa's upcoming Hull home match in Gameweek 5 and Coventry away in Gameweek 6 offer enough fixture upside to justify patience rather than another immediate transfer.
key_points: Cole Palmer is the Gameweek 4 captain, with his lower ownership making him more appealing than João Pedro.
Erling Haaland is held without question and is planned as captain for Manchester City's Gameweek 5 home fixture against Sunderland.
David Raya, Calafiori and Conso make up an aggressive Arsenal defensive triple-up targeting a Sunderland clean sheet.
De Cuyper remains a useful pick while he continues to play at left wing until Mitoma returns.
Morgan Rogers replaces Rayan Cherki after a move made before Rogers reaches £7.6m, primarily because Cherki's minutes look unreliable.
Szoboszlai is retained for the Fulham fixture, while Gross is favoured against Coventry.
Wissa is kept despite his Gameweek 3 blank because Hull at home in Gameweek 5 and Coventry away in Gameweek 6 provide a favourable short-term run.

items.title: FPL GW4 EXPERTS TEAM 🚀 430x Top 10k! 💥 BEST WILDCARD + FREE HIT!
items.headline: Palmer dominates Gameweek 4 captaincy as elite managers pile into Chelsea attack
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the overwhelming Gameweek 4 captaincy pick among leading FPL managers, backed by 72% despite Hull having kept three straight clean sheets. Chelsea’s attacking output makes the fixture hard to ignore: Palmer scores twice after coming off the bench in the cup, while Morgan Rogers records four assists in the same match and has returned in all three league gameweeks. João Pedro is the main alternative captain at 22%, with Erling Haaland, Bruno Fernandes, Rogers and Alexander Isak attracting only isolated support. Most triple-captain users back Palmer; one notable exception instead triples Isak against a Fulham side ranked 19th for expected goals conceded.

Rogers is the standout transfer target, bought by 64% of the top managers, with Palmer second and Arsenal budget defender Constant also heavily recruited after an impressive European debut at £4.4m. Palmer and Rogers are viewed as the priority buys for managers without Chelsea coverage, while João Pedro remains widely backed. Arsenal assets continue to appeal after their defensive dominance and strong underlying numbers, with David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori, Conor and Saka featuring regularly in elite squads. Calafiori’s advanced positioning, Conor’s ownership surge and Arsenal’s defensive security make a double-up at the back a popular route.

The most common moves in the experts’ team are Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire and Dominic Calvert-Lewin out, with Palmer, Rogers, Conor and Whiston in. The resulting Gameweek 4 XI is Kinsky; Califiori, Diper and Conor; Rogers, Palmer, Szoboszlai and Gross; Haaland, Whiston and João Pedro, with around £1m spare. Palmer, Rogers, Gross and Conor all carry notably higher ownership among elite managers than in the overall game, while Bruno has a substantial negative expert-ownership gap and is a potential sell for those needing Chelsea attackers. However, some strong managers retain Bruno, believing he offers captaincy potential in Gameweeks 6 and 8 as his ownership falls.

Chip use is unusually aggressive: 25% of the tracked managers have unlimited transfers active, including roughly 20% on Wildcard and 5% on Free Hit, while 7% use Triple Captain. One Wildcard prioritises a more balanced medium-term squad over a one-week Free Hit, pairing Palmer and Rogers with Saka, Mbeumo, Haaland, João Pedro and Barry. The reasoning is to attack Hull while avoiding an excessive Chelsea commitment, retain Saka as a Gameweek 6 captaincy option and exploit Arsenal’s defence. A Free Hit squad, meanwhile, leans fully into Raya, Calafiori, Chelsea’s Palmer-Rogers-João Pedro core, Liverpool’s Szoboszlai and Isak, and attacking defenders such as Diper and Vuskovic. The main caution is that the Triple Captain chip has relatively limited season-long value, so even a Palmer blank is not considered season-defining.
key_points: Cole Palmer is captained by 72% of elite managers for Chelsea v Hull in Gameweek 4, with João Pedro the clear second choice on 22%.
Morgan Rogers is the leading transfer in, bought by 64% after two goals and an assist across the first three gameweeks and four cup assists off the bench.
Palmer and Rogers are viewed as the urgent buys for teams without Chelsea coverage, although Hull’s three consecutive clean sheets add risk to a Chelsea triple-up.
Conor becomes a major budget-defender target, with 58% elite ownership versus 14% overall, while Calafiori and Raya sustain strong Arsenal defensive interest.
Bruno Fernandes is the most notable potential sell, but some managers hold him for captaincy opportunities in Gameweeks 6 and 8.
Around 20% of tracked managers activate Wildcard in Gameweek 4, 5% use Free Hit and 7% play Triple Captain, almost entirely on Palmer.
Alexander Isak is a differential Triple Captain option against Fulham, whose defence is rated poorly for expected goals conceded and big chances allowed.
Cody Gakpo is heavily bought overall but carries an adductor concern and uncertain availability for Gameweek 4.

items.title: FPL GW4 Transfer Tips! | Buy, Sell, Keep, Avoid #fpl
items.headline: Cole Palmer becomes the standout Gameweek 4 buy and captaincy gamble against Hull
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the priority transfer for Gameweek 4 as Chelsea face Hull, with captaincy also a viable aggressive move. Hull remain unbeaten defensively on the surface, but their underlying defensive numbers are among the league’s poorest, suggesting Chelsea’s attacking quality can expose them. João Pedro and Morgan Rogers are also identified as high-priority targets for managers unable to reach Palmer or needing cheaper attacking additions.

Ryan Cherki is the recommended sale after his Manchester City punt against Coventry fails to deliver. City’s influx of attacking signings, combined with a heavier schedule across competitions, makes their midfield and forward options increasingly difficult to trust for starts. Cherki, Phil Foden, Enzo, Nico O’Reilly and other City attackers have quality, but their rotation risk undermines their FPL appeal unless their minutes become more secure.

Dominik Szoboszlai is a firm hold despite blanking in Gameweek 3. He is unfortunate to have two strong efforts saved by Ipswich goalkeeper Shèrpen and a penalty ruled out for a marginal offside, while Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak benefit from goalkeeper errors. Szoboszlai retains reliable minutes, set-piece responsibility, occasional penalty potential and encouraging open-play threat, making him attractive against a leaky Fulham defence.

Managers are advised not to buy Anthony Elanga, Harvey Barnes or, for non-owners, Yoane Wissa this week. Newcastle’s attack is not consistently creating clear-cut chances, and a handful of exceptional individual goals masks underlying overperformance. With Leeds United offering a tougher defensive test, the recommendation is to wait until Gameweek 5, when Newcastle meet Hull, before reassessing their attacking assets.
key_points: Buy Cole Palmer for Chelsea’s Gameweek 4 match against Hull, with captaincy a realistic upside play.
João Pedro and Morgan Rogers are alternative high-priority transfers for managers who cannot reach Palmer.
Sell Ryan Cherki as Manchester City’s growing attacking depth and fixture load make his minutes too uncertain.
Avoid relying on City attackers such as Foden, Enzo and O’Reilly unless there is clearer evidence of secure starts.
Keep Dominik Szoboszlai: he has set pieces, possible penalties, secure minutes and a strong Gameweek 4 fixture against Fulham.
Do not buy Anthony Elanga, Harvey Barnes or Yoane Wissa before Newcastle face Leeds; reassess Newcastle assets for the Gameweek 5 trip to Hull.

items.title: 'I HAD TO MAKE THIS TRANSFER' ⚪️ | FPL Harry's GW4 Team Selection
items.headline: Milenkovic over White and Konsa is a calculated two-week defensive punt
items.summary:
Nikola Milenkovic replaces Joe Rodon after a weak defence makes a transfer unavoidable. The move is made before Arsenal’s line-up is confirmed, and in hindsight Ben White or Ezri Konsa may have been the safer alternatives.

Milenkovic is backed for Nottingham Forest’s home matches against Newcastle and Crystal Palace, where his clean-sheet potential, defensive-contribution upside and threat from set pieces offer multiple routes to returns. The appeal is not solely dependent on Forest keeping two clean sheets.

The gamble is that Arsenal do not deliver consecutive shutouts. If an Arsenal defender returns a clean sheet in one match but little in the other, a points split such as six and two could be matched by Milenkovic producing steady four-point returns across both fixtures. Konsa and White may look preferable with the benefit of the confirmed information, but Milenkovic is viewed as capable of matching Konsa over the next two gameweeks.
key_points: Nikola Milenkovic comes in for Joe Rodon because the defence needs immediate strengthening.
Ben White and Ezri Konsa are acknowledged as possible alternatives, particularly after Arsenal’s line-up becomes clear.
Milenkovic has home fixtures against Newcastle and Crystal Palace across the next two gameweeks.
The Forest defender offers clean-sheet potential, defensive-contribution points and attacking threat from set pieces.
The transfer relies on Arsenal failing to keep two clean sheets, allowing Milenkovic’s steadier returns to compete with White or Konsa.

items.title: MY FPL GW4 TEAM SELECTION! 📱3x TRANSFERS CONFIRMED... BUT WHY? 👀 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Cole Palmer edges Haaland for Gameweek 4 captaincy as FPL squad holds wildcard
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the preferred captain for Gameweek 4 after Chelsea’s attacking performance in the 6-3 win over Leeds, with João Pedro vice-captain against Hull at Stamford Bridge. Palmer scores twice, takes a penalty and looks sharp alongside Morgan Rogers, who supplies four assists after coming on. Hull are yet to concede in the league, but Chelsea’s home attack appears strong enough to overcome that resistance. Erling Haaland, away to Manchester United, remains a credible alternative but Palmer’s penalty duty, midfielder goal points and clean-sheet point give him the edge.

Three transfers are already confirmed: Bruno Fernandes becomes Palmer, Rodon becomes West Ham defender Konstantinos Mavropanos, and Solanke becomes Morgan Gibbs-White. Palmer is selected over a cheaper Chelsea route such as Rogers because the plan is only for the short stretch before a likely Gameweek 6 wildcard, and the premium midfielder offers the highest explosive upside against Hull and Brentford. Gibbs-White is preferred to Rogers to avoid a triple Chelsea attack and to target Aston Villa away and Coventry at home; he has set pieces, penalties and Forest’s strongest open-play goal threat. However, Rogers’ four-assist display means he now looks a serious alternative and may prove the better short-term pick.

Mavropanos is chosen over Ezri Konsa or Ben White despite the appeal of doubling up on Arsenal’s defence for Sunderland away and Brighton away. The move is made early to avoid Rodon’s price fall and protect squad value before the Arsenal team news is known. Mavropanos has Newcastle and Crystal Palace at home, offers strong defensive-contribution potential and carries some set-piece threat. The risk is clear: Arsenal’s defence looks capable of consecutive clean sheets, but one Mavropanos clean sheet plus defensive points would make the short-term gamble acceptable.

The wildcard is held for Gameweek 6 rather than activated now. A wildcard squad would likely add a second Arsenal defender, replace Dominik Szoboszlai with a stronger Liverpool or midfield option, and possibly move Dominic Calvert-Lewin to Yoane Wissa. But none of those upgrades feels sufficiently decisive over the next two gameweeks to justify using the chip early. Saving it through the international break allows more time for injuries, form and selection patterns to emerge, while a rolled transfer in Gameweek 5 can preserve flexibility.

The starting XI includes Verbruggen over Kinsky in goal, Calafiori and Mavropanos in defence, and Bryan Mbeumo ahead of Gomez despite Mbeumo facing Manchester City. Mbeumo’s form and underlying numbers, including the second-highest expected goals among midfielders, outweigh Gomez’s better Coventry fixture. Haaland, Calvert-Lewin and João Pedro lead the attack, while Szoboszlai stays for Fulham at home and Bournemouth away before the prospective wildcard. The earlier Haaland triple-captain return of nine points is viewed as disappointing but not damaging: the chip’s true lost upside versus ordinary Haaland captaincy is limited, and larger weekly gains can be found through routine selection calls.
key_points: Cole Palmer is the Gameweek 4 captain against Hull, with João Pedro vice-captain and Erling Haaland an alternative away to Manchester United.
Confirmed transfers are Bruno Fernandes to Palmer, Rodon to Konstantinos Mavropanos, and Solanke to Morgan Gibbs-White.
Mavropanos is a short-term punt for Newcastle and Crystal Palace at home, prioritising defensive-contribution and goal threat over an Arsenal defensive double-up.
Gibbs-White gets the nod over Morgan Rogers because of penalties, set pieces, Forest’s fixtures and the desire not to own three Chelsea attackers, although Rogers’ four assists raise doubts.
The wildcard is pencilled in for Gameweek 6 over the international break, with double Arsenal defence and Yoane Wissa among the likely upgrades.
Bryan Mbeumo starts against Manchester City over Gomez against Coventry due to his excellent early-season form and elite expected-goals numbers.
Verbruggen starts over Kinsky, while Calvert-Lewin and Szoboszlai are retained for the next two fixtures before the possible wildcard.
Haaland’s nine-point triple-captain score is treated as acceptable because the effective difference from a future regular Haaland captaincy haul is relatively small.

items.title: My FPL Team for GW4 🔥 1 Transfer made 👀
items.headline: Cole Palmer is the differential captain as Rogers replaces Cherki for Gameweek 4
items.summary:
After a disappointing 44-point Wildcard week that drops his rank from 57,000 to 203,000, the squad remains built around a strong short-term fixture run rather than a late Wildcard reset. The key move is an early transfer from Cherki to Morgan Rogers, made before Rogers rises to £7.6m. Cherki could continue to start for Manchester City, but his 60-to-70-minute outings and longer-term rotation risk make him a likely problem, while Rogers is expected to start against Hull, regularly play 80-plus minutes and retain a favourable run beyond Gameweek 4.

Cole Palmer is set to captain Chelsea at home to Hull, ahead of team-mate João Pedro and Erling Haaland away to Manchester United. Palmer plays only 45 minutes in the midweek cup match and is expected to start, while his lower ownership than João Pedro gives the captaincy extra upside. The Triple Captain chip is under serious consideration for Palmer as a high-risk differential, although it is not activated yet. Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7 and Hull in Gameweek 16 remain alternative chip opportunities, while potential weather-related postponements could yet make a Free Hit more valuable than a Triple Captain.

The defence stays unchanged, with Raya, Calafiori and Konsa forming a triple Arsenal defensive investment for Sunderland. Arsenal's underlying defensive numbers are strong, with less than 0.5 xG conceded in each league match so far, and Calafiori's midweek rest increases confidence that he starts. De Cuyper is expected to continue at left wing against Coventry while Mitoma is absent, with Lewis Hall and Gvardiol providing bench cover. The £1.1m in the bank is deliberately preserved for a future upgrade when De Cuyper loses his place or Gvardiol's minutes become less secure.

Haaland, João Pedro and Yoane Wissa all keep their places up front. Haaland is not under consideration for sale and is already pencilled in as captain for Sunderland at home in Gameweeks 5 and 7, while Wissa is given at least three more weeks to prove himself despite concerns that he is operating too deeply. With one free transfer remaining, the preference is to roll rather than reactively replace Gvardiol or chase a Spurs defender. The priority is reaching the international break after Gameweek 5 with three free transfers, even if that means retaining a potentially imperfect option such as Sangaré for one more week.
key_points: Morgan Rogers replaces Cherki early, before Rogers rises to £7.6m, because Rogers offers safer starts and stronger expected minutes against Hull and beyond.
Cole Palmer is the planned Gameweek 4 captain at home to Hull, chosen as a lower-owned differential over João Pedro and Haaland.
A Palmer Triple Captain is tempting but remains undecided; Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7 or Hull in Gameweek 16 are the main alternatives.
Raya, Calafiori and Konsa start in a triple Arsenal defence against Sunderland, backed by Arsenal's elite early-season defensive data.
Calafiori's midweek rest makes him a strong starter, while De Cuyper is expected to keep his place until Mitoma returns.
Haaland stays despite Manchester United away in Gameweek 4 and is the planned captain for Sunderland at home in Gameweeks 5 and 7.
Wissa is retained through his fixtures against Leeds, Hull and Coventry before any reassessment of his role and output.
The remaining free transfer is likely rolled, with the aim of carrying three free transfers into the post-Gameweek 5 international break.

items.title: FPL GW4 EXPERT Wildcard Team & Transfer Trends! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 4 Team Plans
items.headline: Cole Palmer dominates Gameweek 4 plans as experts overhaul squads on Wildcards
items.summary:
Gameweek 4 brings a major expert-led reshuffle, with 35% of the 100 surveyed managers activating a Wildcard and a further 2% using a Free Hit. Only 11% make no move, while most non-chip managers target Chelsea and Arsenal assets. Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa are the overwhelming free-transfer priorities, while Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Rayan Cherki, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are among the most common sales ahead of the Manchester derby.

Palmer is the defining pick of the week. He appears in every one of the 35 expert Wildcard drafts and is also captained by 70% of the sample for Chelsea's home fixture against Hull City. João Pedro is the clear fallback captain at 18%, while Erling Haaland receives only 8% backing despite his usual premium appeal. All of the experts using Triple Captain place it on Palmer, although only 4% of the overall group deploy the chip, suggesting many still prefer to save it for a later high-upside week.

The Wildcard template is built around Palmer, Rogers, João Pedro and Haaland, with Riccardo Calafiori and Konsa virtually universal defensive selections at 97% each. Egan-Riley is the preferred £4.0m defender, while Muharemovic and Lewis Hall provide popular additional options. In goal, Kinsky leads the way, ahead of David Raya and Verbruggen, generally paired with a £4.0m reserve. The key Arsenal structure is Calafiori and Konsa plus either Saka or Raya; Saka is marginally more popular, but the Raya-and-Morgan Gibbs-White alternative offers a similarly priced route.

Midfield choices beyond Palmer and Rogers are less settled. Gross is selected in around two-thirds of Wildcards, while Saka, Gibbs-White and Gakpo are viable alternatives. Experts are notably cooler on Gakpo than the wider FPL market: despite being the most-bought player overall, he is included in only 26% of Wildcards, partly because Liverpool's schedule stiffens after Fulham in Gameweek 4. Up front, the third striker slot is the main compromise: Wissa remains the most common choice but falls sharply from his previous near-essential status, with Barry and Gonzalo competing as cheaper alternatives. Bruno Fernandes is in only 9% of Wildcards, underlining the willingness to move away from Manchester United assets for the upcoming fixture swing.
key_points: Cole Palmer is in 100% of expert Wildcards and is the captaincy favourite for Chelsea at home to Hull City, backed by 70% of experts.
Palmer is the only Triple Captain pick in the survey, but just 4% of experts use the chip in Gameweek 4.
Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa join Palmer as the standout non-Wildcard transfer targets.
Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Rayan Cherki, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are major sales as managers reduce Manchester exposure before the derby.
Riccardo Calafiori and Konsa are selected by 97% of Wildcard teams, with Egan-Riley the preferred budget defender.
João Pedro and Erling Haaland are in 100% and 97% respectively of expert Wildcards; the third forward is split between Wissa, Barry and Gonzalo.
Experts show limited enthusiasm for Cody Gakpo despite his popularity in the wider market, with only 26% selecting him on a Wildcard.
The main Arsenal decision is Saka versus Raya: Saka is slightly more popular, while Raya can fund a midfield alternative such as Morgan Gibbs-White.

items.title: FPL GW4 WILDCARD DRAFT! 🍟 #fpl  #premierleague
items.headline: Wildcard draft for Gameweek 4 backs Arsenal defensive triple-up and João Pedro captaincy
items.summary:
A Gameweek 4 Wildcard draft prioritises defensive value, led by David Raya and an intended triple-up on Arsenal’s back line. Calvin Bassey is included for his attacking potential, while Ibrahima Konaté is viewed as underpriced at £4.4m. The trade-off is that three Arsenal defensive slots prevent investment in Arsenal attackers such as Bukayo Saka, Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz, but Arsenal’s defensive outlook is considered strong enough to justify it. Joël Veltman is another attacking-minded defensive option, with Coventry away next, while Malick Thiaw and John Egan provide cheap bench cover for favourable upcoming fixtures.

Midfield is built around flexibility rather than immediately owning Bruno Fernandes. Bryan Mbeumo earns a place after scoring in each of the previous two matches, while Cole Palmer is preferred to Morgan Rogers because his price point makes future moves to premium midfielders easier. Palmer can be sold to reach Bruno Fernandes or Saka in the coming weeks without requiring a major squad restructure. Pascal Groß and Morgan Gibbs-White complete the main midfield options, with Gibbs-White particularly appealing for matches against Aston Villa, Coventry and Crystal Palace over the next three gameweeks; Sangaré is retained as a bench option.

Erling Haaland and João Pedro are treated as near-essential forwards, especially in a structure that excludes Bruno Fernandes. Yoane Wissa completes the attack. Captaincy is placed on João Pedro, with Palmer as vice-captain, reflecting the desire to target Chelsea’s attacking potential in Gameweek 4. Managers who have already made transfers can still activate the Wildcard later in the week, with those free transfers restored for Gameweek 5.
key_points: The Gameweek 4 Wildcard uses David Raya plus a defensive triple-up strategy focused on Arsenal’s strong defensive appeal.
Calvin Bassey is selected for attacking threat, while Ibrahima Konaté is considered excellent value at £4.4m.
The Arsenal defensive commitment blocks routes to Bukayo Saka, Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz, making it a high-conviction structural choice.
Cole Palmer is preferred to Morgan Rogers because he provides an easier future route to Bruno Fernandes or Saka.
Bryan Mbeumo is backed after scoring in his previous two matches, while Morgan Gibbs-White has a favourable three-match run against Aston Villa, Coventry and Crystal Palace.
Haaland and João Pedro are viewed as forward-line locks, with Yoane Wissa completing the frontline.
João Pedro is the Gameweek 4 captain, with Palmer vice-captain.
Activating the Wildcard after making transfers later in the week restores those free transfers for Gameweek 5.
